newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Texaco exec Lundwall charged. [CORRECTED 20:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ex-Texaco exec Lundwall charged. [CORRECTED 20:30 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and throughout to make clear that Lundwall was charged but not indicted.)

Former Texaco executive Richard Lundwall is to be arraigned in federal court in White Plains, New York at around 1300 EST/1800 GMT in the ongoing racial bias case surrounding Texaco, a spokesman at the U.S. Attorney's office said.
Asked whether there would be any further arrests in the case, Marvin Smilon said "the investigation is continuing."
Lundwall was charged with obstruction of justice, Smilon said.
According to a copy of the complaint obtained by Reuters, Lundwall "unlawfully, willingly, and knowingly...corruptly destroyed, concealed, and withheld documents" in the civil lawsuit.
Lundwall was former senior coordinator of personnel services in Texaco's finance department.
A person answering a phone call at Texaco said the
company's media officials were in a meeting, and not available to comment on the former official being charged.
The charges come four days after the announcement that Texaco had reached a $176 million settlement of a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by six black employees in 1994.
